messages.content: The /app directory is empty, so I need to create /app/regex.txt. My plan: build a line-anchored regex of the form `^(?=.*<valid IPv4>).*(<valid date>)` where the greedy `.*` forces the last valid date on the line, and re.findall returns the single capturing group (the date). Dates must validate month/day ranges (Feb up to 29, 30-day months up to 30, 31-day months up to 31) and have non-alphanumeric boundaries. IPv4 octets are 0-255 without leading zeros, also with non-alphanumeric boundaries. First, let me write the regex file.

The regex is written. Now I need to thoroughly test it with a Python script covering valid/invalid dates, IPv4 boundaries, multiple dates (last one should match), and false-positive traps like 'user 1134-12-1234'.
Test script written. Run it to verify the regex behaves as expected.

All tests passed except '2024-11-30T22:10:00' — but actually my test expectation was wrong: the date is followed by 'T' (alphanumeric), and the spec explicitly says valid dates must NOT be immediately followed by alphanumeric characters. So the regex correctly rejects it. I'll fix that expectation and add more edge cases to be thorough.

action.summary:
Saved the regex to /app/regex.txt. The pattern is:

^(?=.*(?<![0-9a-zA-Z])(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9][0-9]|[1-9]?[0-9])\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9][0-9]|[1-9]?[0-9])(?![0-9a-zA-Z])).*(?<![0-9a-zA-Z])([0-9]{4}-(?:(?:0[13578]|1[02])-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])|(?:0[469]|11)-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|30)|02-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-9])))(?![0-9a-zA-Z])

How it works:
- `^` anchors each line (re.MULTILINE), so one match per line.
- The lookahead requires the line to contain a valid IPv4 address: octets 0-255 with no leading zeros (`25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9][0-9]|[1-9]?[0-9]`), not immediately preceded/followed by alphanumeric characters.
- The greedy `.*` before the date forces the match to be the LAST valid date in the line.
- The single capturing group matches YYYY-MM-DD with full calendar validation: months 01-12; 31-day months (01,03,05,07,08,10,12) allow days 01-31; 30-day months (04,06,09,11) allow 01-30; February allows 01-29 in all years. Lookaround boundaries prevent false matches like 'user 1134-12-1234' or dates embedded in alphanumeric text.
- Since there is exactly one capturing group, re.findall returns only the date strings.

Verified with 59 test cases covering all edge cases, plus realistic multi-line log simulation and Unicode-digit rejection; all pass.
